chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, Muḥammad ibn Muslim, and Abū Baṣīr, who said: We said to him: There is a well from which wudu (ablution) is performed, and urine flows near it; does it make it impure? He said:

So he said: “If the well is at the upper part of the valley, and the valley in which urine flows runs below it, and between them there is a distance of three cubits or four cubits, that does not render it impure in any way. But if the well is at the lower part of the valley and the water passes over it, and between the well and it there are nine cubits, it does not render it impure; and whatever is less than that, wudu (ablution) is not to be performed from it.”

Zurārah said: So I said to him: Then what if it flows right next to it and does not remain upon the ground? He said: “So long as it has no settled standing, there is no problem with it. If a little of it settles, then it does not pierce the earth nor penetrate through it until it reaches the well, and there is no harm upon the well from it, so perform wudu (ablution) from it. That only applies if all of it becomes pooled.”

key_terms.أَذْرُعٍ: cubits, a unit of distance used to determine legal separation
key_terms.اسْتَنْقَعَ: became pooled or collected in one place
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine, the impure substance discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْبِئْرُ: the well from which water is drawn for ritual use
key_terms.الْوَادِي: the valley or channel through which liquid flows
key_terms.قَرَارٌ: a settled standing or stable resting of liquid

ai.seo_question: When does nearby flowing impurity make well water unfit for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the purity of well water when nearby urine flows in a valley. It explains that distance, elevation, and whether the impurity settles or pools affect whether the well remains suitable for wudu (ablution). The narration is significant in fiqh for determining ritual purity and the practical limits of contamination.
